title: KOSPI/KOSDAQ Market Close, Sep 30, 2026: Foreign Selling Erases Chip-Led Rally
content:
Korea Supply Chain Brief · Market Close, September 30, 2026

KOSPI closed at 6,837.83, down 0.48%, while KOSDAQ closed at 855.92, up 0.72%, as an early rally on a U.S. semiconductor rebound gave way to heavy foreign selling through the session. Here is what moved the market today.

What moved today

Chip rebound opens strong, then foreign selling erases the gain

Despite ongoing pressure from rising U.S. long-term Treasury yields, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 1.32% overnight and Micron and SK hynix ADRs advanced, sending KOSPI more than 1% higher at the open, briefly touching the 6,950 level. Foreign and institutional selling accelerated through the session, however, erasing most of the gain and briefly pushing the index negative before the close. Foreign investors have been net sellers in the Korean market for an extended stretch, and tonight's Micron earnings report is widely seen as a key signal for near-term memory chip demand, which added to volatility across individual names. (Market move, sentiment-driven)

Steel pipe and valve makers surge on report of possible $54B Alaska LNG investment

Shares of steel pipe and valve makers jumped after foreign media reported that U.S. President Trump may announce a Korean investment of roughly $54 billion tied to the Alaska LNG development project as part of a broader announcement on Korea-U.S. investment on September 30 local time. The project would move natural gas from the North Slope through roughly 1,300 km of pipeline to southern Alaska, a scale that could generate substantial demand for steel pipe. Dongil Steel Lux and KBI Dongyang Steel Pipe hit their daily upper limit, and buying spread to TCC Steel, Keumkang Steel, Hi Steel, Hwasung Valve, Hyusteel, and Nexteel. The Korean government currently classifies Alaska LNG as a matter "for future discussion," so the $54 billion figure is not yet confirmed — today's move reflects positioning ahead of a possible announcement rather than a finalized deal. (Reported)

Bloom Energy's 10%+ rally lifts Korean fuel cell names

U.S. fuel cell maker Bloom Energy rallied more than 10%, drawing buying into Korean fuel cell suppliers tied to its value chain. The move follows Bloom Energy securing a new 158,000-square-foot facility in Fremont, California to expand production capacity, alongside continued expectations for SOFC demand growth from AI data center power needs; Jefferies also raised its price target to $264. Vinatech, Hansun Engineering, Beomhan Fuelcell, Doosan Fuelcell, and Meco advanced on the news. (Market move, sentiment-driven)

Solid-state battery materials gain as commercialization timeline firms up

Solid-state battery development is reported to be shifting from research toward mass-production readiness, lifting expectations for commercial-scale output of core materials including sulfide-based solid electrolyte and lithium sulfide. Isu Specialty Chemical was a standout gainer on the strength of its reported lithium sulfide production technology, a key raw material for sulfide-based solid-state batteries, with Hannong Chemical also advancing on the theme. (Reported)

Glass substrate names rotate higher on Nvidia packaging speculation

As chip packages grow larger and more densely integrated, thermal management and signal-loss limits in conventional organic substrates have kept alive market speculation that Nvidia is evaluating glass substrates for next-generation packaging. Taesung, which entered the glass substrate equipment market building on its PCB automation know-how, is reported to have a lineup covering roughly 17 processes and to have expanded production capacity roughly sixfold through a new plant. Combined with Philoptics' recent order for 2.0mm glass substrate TGV equipment marking an actual commercialization step, YC Chem, Philoptics, Taesung, and Tomocube advanced. (Reported)

Broader semiconductor equipment and materials names advanced on Micron earnings anticipation

Ahead of tonight's scheduled Micron earnings report, anticipation of a broader memory market recovery drew pre-positioning buying into Korean semiconductor equipment and materials names. Micron's overnight gain and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index's rise lifted Samsung Electronics and SK hynix early in the session, with buying spreading to front-end process, materials, specialty gas, and inspection equipment makers including Jusung Engineering, TEMC, Foosung, and Soulbrain. Tonight's report is expected to be watched less for headline revenue than for HBM and server DRAM demand, memory pricing, and capex guidance, all of which could shape investor sentiment toward Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, and the broader supplier base. (Market move, sentiment-driven)

Quick FAQ

Why did KOSPI give back its early gain today?
A U.S. semiconductor rebound drove KOSPI more than 1% higher at the open, but accelerating foreign and institutional selling through the session erased most of that gain by the close.

Is the $54 billion Alaska LNG investment confirmed?
No. The Korean government classifies it as a matter for future discussion; today's rally in steel pipe and valve names reflects positioning ahead of a possible announcement, not a finalized deal.

Why does tonight's Micron earnings report matter for Korean stocks?
HBM and server DRAM demand, memory pricing, and capex guidance in the report could shape sentiment toward Samsung Electronics, SK hynix, and the broader Korean semiconductor equipment and materials supply chain.
